title: Phones, apps & payments
goal: Sort out credit, data and wifi, talk about apps, updates and passwords, order online and pay or send money from your phone, and talk about social media — using English tech words with Pashto grammar.
intro:
Tech talk in Pashto is half English: you **ډاونلوډ** an app, **اپډېټ** your phone and **لايک** a post. What makes it Pashto is the verb that comes after: **کول** 'do' when you do it, **کېدل** 'become' when it happens by itself — ډاونلوډ يې **کړه** 'download it', ټيلفون مې هنګ **شو** 'my phone froze'. And because کول is transitive, the past is ergative, just like every other verb you know: عکسونه مې ډيلېټ **کړل**.

You'll also get plenty of practice with **که** 'if' in real situations — if the code doesn't come, if you've sent the money, if there's wifi — and the words for credit, data bundles, delivery and mobile money that people in Kabul and Peshawar use every day.

grammar.title: English word + کول or کېدل
grammar.body:
Pashto takes English tech words as they are and makes them into verbs with **کول** 'do' (someone does it *to* something) or **کېدل** 'become' (it *happens*, by itself):

ډاونلوډ **کول** 'to download (something)' · ډاونلوډ **کېدل** 'to be downloading'
اپډېټ کول / اپډېټ کېدل · انسټال کول · ډيلېټ کول · لايک کول · فالو کول · پوسټ کول · هنګ کېدل 'to freeze'.

They work exactly like پاک کول and جوړ کېدل, which you already know:
• **Present**: اپ ډاونلوډ **کوم** 'I'm downloading the app' · ټيلفون هنګ **کېږي** 'the phone keeps freezing'.
• **Commands, subjunctive, future**: کول → **کړ-**, کېدل → **ش-**: انسټال يې **کړه** 'install it' · کله چې اپډېټ **شي** 'when it's updated'. 'Don't': پوسټ يې **مه کوه**.
• **Past with کول is ergative**: the doer is oblique or a clitic, and **کړ / کړه / کړل** agrees with the thing: ما اپ ډيلېټ **کړ** (m) · شمېره مې ډيلېټ **کړه** (f) · عکسونه مې ډيلېټ **کړل** (m pl). Even people: زه دې فالو **کړم**؟ 'did you follow me?' (agrees with زه).
• **Past with کېدل** agrees with the subject: ټيلفون هنګ **شو** · اپ اپډېټ **شو**.

**The trap**: کول or کېدل? 'It downloaded' (by itself) is ډاونلوډ **شو**; 'I downloaded it' is ډاونلوډ مې **کړ**. Most loanwords are masculine.

grammar.title: 'If …' in practice: که with the right verb
grammar.body:
You met **که** 'if' in unit 19. With phones and payments you use it all the time, and what matters is the verb in the if-clause:

**1. Something that may happen → که + subjunctive**, then future, imperative or present: که انټرنېټ **راشي**، زنګ به درته ووهم 'if the internet comes back, I'll call you' · که کوډ **رانه شي**، بيا يې وغواړه 'if the code doesn't come, ask for it again'.

**2. A general rule, 'whenever' → که + present**: که وای فای **وي**، ويډيو ګورم 'if there's wifi, I watch videos' · که اکاونټ **نه لرې**، جوړ يې کړه 'if you don't have an account, make one'.

**3. Something that may already have happened → که + past participle + وي**: که دې پيسې **لېږلې وي**، رسيد راته ولېږه 'if you've sent the money, send me the receipt' · که دې اکاونټ جوړ **کړی وي** … 'if you've made an account …'. The participle agrees like any perfect (پيسې f pl → لېږلې).

**4. 'Otherwise'** is **که نه**: ژر يې تاديه کړه، **که نه** آرډر لغوه کېږي 'pay quickly, otherwise the order gets cancelled'.

The if-clause comes first. **نو** 'then' may start the second half, but in speech it is usually dropped. Negatives: نه goes before the verb — in a perfective, after و: که پيسې **ونه** رسېږي 'if the money doesn't arrive'.

culture:
Most people carry **two SIM cards** from different networks, because coverage and bundle prices differ, and top up with scratch cards from any corner shop or through **mobile money**: M-Paisa and HesabPay in Afghanistan, **Easypaisa** and **JazzCash** in Pakistan, used for bills, transfers to family and paying shops. In Pakistan you shop on Daraz and order food on Foodpanda; in both countries **cash on delivery** is still the safest and most common way to pay, and delivery boys on motorbikes are everywhere. Power cuts (in Pakistan, *load-shedding*, لوډشېډنګ) mean the wifi goes off with the lights.

**WhatsApp** is the main channel for everything — family groups, voice notes, work — with IMO popular for calling relatives abroad, Facebook big among older users and TikTok and YouTube among the young. Many people type Pashto in **Latin letters** in chat (*sta sanga ye?*) because Pashto keyboards are fiddly, and they freely mix in English: *download, update, password, account, online, like, follow*. Pashto has official coinages — **برېښناليک** for email, **ټولنيزې رسنۍ** for social media — that you'll hear on the news and see in formal writing, but in conversation the English word plus **کول** is what people really say.

tip.title: When the connection is bad
tip.body:
- **انټرنېټ نه چلېږي** 'the internet isn't working'; **سست دی** 'it's slow'; **ګډوډ دی** 'it's playing up'.
- Credit: **کرېډټ اچول** 'to top up'; **کرېډټ مې خلاص شو** 'I've run out'.
- Data: **بسته اخيستل** 'to buy a bundle'.
- In Pakistan: بيلنس for credit, پېکېج for a bundle.

tip.title: English word + کول / کېدل
tip.body:
- You do it: **کول** — ډاونلوډ يې **کړه** 'download it'.
- It happens: **کېدل** — اپډېټ **کېږي** 'it's updating', هنګ **شو** 'it froze'.
- Past with کول is ergative and agrees with the thing: اپ مې ډيلېټ **کړ**، عکسونه مې ډيلېټ **کړل**.
tip.pattern: ډاونلوډ کول (you do it) · ډاونلوډ کېدل (it happens)

tip.title: 'If …': که + the right verb
tip.body:
- May happen: **که + subjunctive**: که کوډ **رانه شي** …
- General rule: **که + present**: که وای فای **وي** …
- May already have happened: **که + participle + وي**: که دې اکاونټ جوړ **کړی وي** …
- 'Otherwise' = **که نه**.

tip.title: Ordering and delivery
tip.body:
- **آنلاين اخيستل** 'to buy online', **آرډر کول** 'to order'.
- Ask: **ډلېوري وړيا ده؟** and **د ډلېوري فيس څومره دی؟**
- Cash on delivery is still the usual way to pay: **د ډلېوري پر وخت نغدې پيسې ورکول**.

sentences.en: They don't charge a fee — delivery's free.

sentences.native: پيسې به د ډلېوري پر وخت نغدې ورکړم.
sentences.roman: páyse ba də ḍilewarí pər waxt naġdé wárkṛəm.
sentences.en: I'll pay cash on delivery.

tip.title: Paying from your phone
tip.body:
- Pay: **تاديه کول** (formal) or just **پيسې ورکول**.
- Send: **پيسې لېږل** or **ټرانسفر کول** — past is ergative, پيسې is f pl: پيسې مې **ولېږلې**، ټرانسفر مې **کړې**.
- Mobile money: M-Paisa, HesabPay (Afghanistan), Easypaisa, JazzCash (Pakistan).
- Always keep the **رسيد** or a screenshot.

sentences.native: د برېښنا پيسې مې آنلاين ورکړې.
sentences.roman: də breṣnā́ páyse me ānlā́yn wárkṛe.
sentences.en: I paid the electricity bill online.

sentences.native: تاديه وشوه؟
sentences.roman: tādiyá wə́shwa?
sentences.en: Has the payment gone through?

sentences.native: تاديه لا نه ده شوې.
sentences.roman: tādiyá lā na da shə́we.
sentences.en: The payment hasn't gone through yet.

sentences.native: پيسې مې ورور ته ټرانسفر کړې.
sentences.roman: páyse me wror ta ṭrānsfár kṛe.
sentences.en: I transferred the money to my brother.

sentences.native: پيسې درته ورسېدې؟
sentences.roman: páyse dərta wə́rasede?
sentences.en: Has the money reached you?

sentences.native: نه، لا نه دي رسېدلې.
sentences.roman: na, lā na di rasedə́le.
sentences.en: No, it hasn't arrived yet.

sentences.native: په کارت تاديه کوم که نغد؟
sentences.roman: pə kārt tādiyá kawə́m ka naġd?
sentences.en: Shall I pay by card or cash?

sentences.native: د ټرانسفر رسيد راته ولېږه.
sentences.roman: də ṭrānsfár rasíd rā́ta wə́leẓa.
sentences.en: Send me the transfer receipt.

sentences.native: که پيسې ونه رسېږي، زنګ راته ووهه.
sentences.roman: ka páyse wə́na raseẓi, zang rā́ta wə́waha.
sentences.en: If the money doesn't arrive, call me.

tip.title: Like, follow, post
tip.body:
- **لايک کول، فالو کول، پوسټ کول** — all with کول.
- Past is ergative and agrees with the thing: پوسټ مې لايک **کړ**، عکسونه مې لايک **کړل**.
- Even with people: زه دې فالو **کړم**؟ 'did you follow me?'
- Don't: پوسټ يې **مه کوه**.

sentences.native: زما نوی پوسټ دې لايک کړ؟
sentences.roman: zmā náway posṭ de lāyk kaṛ?
sentences.en: Did you like my new post?

sentences.native: ما يې ټول عکسونه لايک کړل.
sentences.roman: mā ye ṭol aksúna lāyk kṛəl.
sentences.en: I liked all her photos.

sentences.native: هغه ډېر خلک فالو کوي.
sentences.roman: haġá ḍer xálək fāló kawí.
sentences.en: He follows loads of people.

sentences.native: زه دې فالو کړم؟
sentences.roman: zə de fāló kṛəm?
sentences.en: Did you follow me?

sentences.native: پروفايل عکس دې بدل کړ؟
sentences.roman: profā́yl aks de badál kaṛ?
sentences.en: Have you changed your profile picture?

sentences.native: په ټولنيزو رسنيو کې ډېر وخت تېروم.
sentences.roman: pə ṭolanízo rasaníyo ke ḍer waxt terawə́m.
sentences.en: I spend too much time on social media.

sentences.native: دا ويډيو پوسټ مه کوه!
sentences.roman: dā viḍiyó posṭ ma kawa!
sentences.en: Don't post this video!

sentences.native: د هغې پوسټ ډېر لايکونه واخيستل.
sentences.roman: də haġé posṭ ḍer lāykúna wā́xistəl.
sentences.en: Her post got loads of likes.

sentences.native: زما پروفايل ته وګوره.
sentences.roman: zmā profā́yl ta wə́gora.
sentences.en: Have a look at my profile.

sentences.native: د هغه پوسټ مې شريک کړ.
sentences.roman: də haġə́ posṭ me sharík kaṛ.
sentences.en: I shared his post.
